title: Reception One Word Hybrid Contextual Launch Foundation

authorized_openings.scope: Provider-free local development of a closed zero-authority Word-to-native-Diary navigation context plus the Reception One request-input visual repair; no patient context, provider call, backend command, confirmation or write.

notes: Yuri selected the Hybrid direction: Word remains the clinical workspace, a later compact companion may summarize admitted work, and detailed Diary work opens in the native Bureau.
The new action is distinct from the ordinary Diary launcher and reuses the existing Office dialog and authentication handshake.
The launch context is kept out of the URL and contains no patient, appointment, request, token, clinical or command field.
The native Diary verifies the requested date before opening Reception One.
Provider, ADC, real/product-derived data, voice, confirmation, writes, production, deployment and release remain closed.

decisions.summary: Preserve Word as the clinical workspace, add a compact Reception One launch surface, and hand detailed work to the authoritative native Diary/Bureau through a closed typed context.

claim_scope: Provider-free Word taskpane launcher and native Diary contextual handoff using one exact non-authoritative typed message.
Verified Diary date movement before Reception One projection opening.
Bounded responsive request-input auto-growth without one- or two-line clipping.
Route-intercepted authored-synthetic local Chromium evidence only; no actual authenticated Word Online, provider, database or production result.

contract_evidence.note: The contextual launch adds no request or patient scope; it preserves the existing Bureau typed-intent and proposal-only contracts.
The launch navigates through the existing verified Diary read path, and the inherited availability reconciliation suite remains green.

unresolved_gates: Actual authenticated Word Online dialog, tenant popup policy and focus restoration require a later supervised product exercise.
The compact conversational Word companion is not implemented by this foundation.
Patient/product-derived context, provider use, voice, confirmation, writes, production, deployment and release remain closed.
